ioc_entries.provenance: helper.pem download URL in the PKGBUILD curl -o line (R001 false trigger)

rules.malicious_reasoning: The fired line is a `curl -o` download that writes a helper PEM into the source directory; there is no pipe to a shell, so it is an ordinary fetch, not a fetch-and-execute pipeline. Ignoring what R001 was meant to catch, the actual behaviour is benign.
rules.reasoning: The added line downloads helper.pem into srcdir and contains no shell pipe (there is no `curl | sh/bash/...` pipeline); it is a normal idiom of fetching an auxiliary file after the source download, so rule R001's curl-to-shell claim does not apply here.
rules.resolution: Tighten R001's regex so that a bare `curl ... -o <url>` download (fetch-to-file, no pipe) does not match; only require the unescaped pipe to be followed by an executable/command token (bash/sh/python/perl/etc.), excluding terminal tokens that are URL-only download targets like `-o https://...`. This stops the false trigger on the `curl -o helper.pem` line while a real fetch-and-exec pipeline keeps firing.
rules.tp_twin: A genuine `curl ... | bash` / `curl ... | sh` / `curl ... | python3` pipeline (unescaped pipe followed by an actual command token) must keep matching.
